decisions.quote: However, the construct validity of this type of IAT has been called into question by recent findings showing that the IAT score implying in-group preference is rather driven by the salience asymmetry within each categorical dyad of the procedure than by evaluative associations between concepts (Rothermund & Wentura, 2001, 2004). In order to assess the validity of an IAT purported to measure French people’s prejudice toward North Africans in France, we conducted two studies that were designed to test the influence of salience asymmetry on an individual’s IAT score.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent (never-adjudicated work). The supplied source is an abstract-only text without a reference list or full text. It jointly cites '(Rothermund & Wentura, 2001, 2004)' for the claim that IAT scores are driven by salience asymmetries rather than evaluative associations, and reports two experiments testing whether salience asymmetries predict French-North African IAT scores. Shipped row input_row_index 2614 (doi_o: 10.1026//0949-3946.48.2.94; Rothermund & Wentura, 2001, 'Figure-Ground Asymmetries in the Implicit Association Test (IAT)') already represents the 2001 target (sibling target_index 0). From the abstract alone, the unresolved questions are: (1) what specific 2004 bibliographic work by Rothermund and Wentura is cited, and (2) whether the paper empirically retests a distinct finding from that 2004 work rather than citing it alongside 2001 as background/theoretical context or an extended report of the 2001 salience-asymmetry paradigm.
